items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: But then I met W. C. Handy on the TOBA.

ctx.x: Senior. Eddie Heywood, Senior. Eddie Heywood, Junior was not around at that time. And from that we went to Memphis... I think we saw Lovey Taylor...was Lovey Taylor a woman piano player? Yeah, I think that was her name. But anyway, we'll check that, so, because I want to be certain there. But then I met W. C. Handy on the TOBA.

It was a very interesting training ground. It was like a Who's Who in America, you know, in black America because if they were anybody, from Georgie Williams and Bessie Brown to Bert Williams to Ma Rainey to Trixie Smith to...well, Ella wasn't around in those days, you know...you know this TOBA was way before. And Joe Bright, and you had...and most of these towns that they played were towns in the Southwest, starting, for example...they had like a circuit, and you'd start in...occasionally in Chicago, but mostly…
